function.name: religion_history_get_councils
function.description: Retrieves a list of major councils in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the councils.

count.description: Number of top councils to retrieve.

function.name: religion_history_get_reformations
function.description: Retrieves a list of major reformations in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: religion_history_get_schisms
function.description: Retrieves a list of major schisms in a specified religion. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

religion.description: Name of the religion for which to retrieve the schisms.

count.description: Number of top schisms to retrieve.

message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Eastern Orthodox Churches (Byzantine Empire) vs. Roman Catholic Church (Western Europe) | Doctrinal differences (e.g., Filioque clause, papal primacy), cultural and political tensions, linguistic barriers, and disputes over liturgical practices. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Reformers (e.g., Martin Luther, John Calvin, Huldrych Zwingli) vs. Roman Catholic Church | Corruption and abuses within the Catholic Church (e.g., indulgences, sale of church offices), theological disputes (e.g., justification by faith alone), and the rise of vernacular scripture and printing technology. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (Ecumenical Movement)** | 1965 CE | Various Christian denominations (including the Catholic, Orthodox, Anglican, Lutheran, and Methodist churches) | Efforts to address theological differences, promote unity, and respond to modern social issues; this “schism” refers more to the ongoing dialogue and occasional disagreements rather than a single event. |

These three events represent the most profound and lasting divisions within Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscapes of their times.
